pages.name: The 5th at 60 Hz
pages.task: A drive on a 60 Hz supply draws a 60 A fundamental, in ideal blocks. What does its 5th harmonic carry?
pages.why: 12 A at 300 Hz. The 5th runs at 5 × 60 = 300 Hz. In ideal blocks it is 1/5 of the fundamental, 60 ÷ 5 = 12 A. Real drives roughly follow this rule.

pages.name: Two harmonics
pages.task: Only the 5th and 7th are present, at 1/5 and 1/7 of the fundamental. What is the THD?
pages.why: About 25%. The 5th is 20% and the 7th 14.3%. Two sines of different frequencies multiply to an average of zero. So only their squares add. √(0.20² + 0.143²) = √0.0604, about 0.25.

pages.task: Drive B is isolated, and its display is dark. You have waited 5 minutes, drive A's time. What is its link at?
pages.why: About 100 V. Drive B's RC is 178 s. So 540 × e^(−300 ÷ 178) is about 100 V. High voltage can be present while an indicator is dark. So wait the time given for that drive, then measure the link.

pages.task: The filter sends nothing to earth while the supply is balanced. Then one supply fuse blows. What flows through earth now?
pages.why: About 7.2 mA. Two equal phasors 120° apart add to one of the same size. So the earth current jumps from nothing to 7.2 mA. The RCD sees all of it.

A phasor diagram of the filter’s capacitor currents. L1 sits at earth. The L2 and L3 currents, 60° apart, add to a large sum that flows through the fault.

pages.task: A drive is fitted on an insulated supply. The insulation monitor alarms each time the drive is switched on, then settles. What is the likeliest cause?
pages.why: Its EMC filter is still connected. The monitor watches the whole connected circuit, drive included. It reads any current between the system and earth as failing insulation. At each switch-on, the filter's capacitors charge through it. So the monitor alarms. The filter would also give a real fault a return path. So disconnect it, as the drive's instructions require.

pages.alt: An earthed 400 V supply feeds a drive through an RCD and fuses. The drive’s EMC filter has a capacitor from each line to earth. All three carry current, and nothing returns through earth. pages.task: A fault inside a three-phase drive, on its DC link, sends DC with little ripple to earth. An RCD protects the circuit against shock. Which type?
pages.why: Type B. Type A detects only sinusoidal AC and pulsating DC. DC from the link barely pulses. For shock protection, a three-phase drive's maker may allow only Type B. Regulation 531.3.3 of BS 7671 sets out the types.

pages.task: Three single-phase rectifier loads share a four-wire supply, one on each line. Each line carries a 10 A 3rd harmonic. What does the neutral carry at 150 Hz?
pages.why: 30 A. The lines are 120° apart at the supply frequency. At three times that frequency, the shift is 360°. So the three 3rds are in step and add in the neutral, 3 × 10 = 30 A. A six-pulse bridge has no neutral, so it draws no 3rd at all.
